questions.prompt: Which property does a cryptographic hash function NOT provide?
questions.explanation: Hashes are deterministic and one-way, but not encrypting — the input is not hidden, just compressed irreversibly.
AES-128 uses 10 rounds. AES-192 uses 12, AES-256 uses 14.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why ECB mode is considered insecure for encrypting structured data.
questions.modelAnswer: ECB encrypts identical plaintext blocks to identical ciphertext blocks, leaking structural patterns of the input.
rubric: Mentions identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks
Mentions pattern leakage / structural information leak
Implies determinism is the root cause
questions.explanation: The classic 'penguin' demonstration: an ECB-encrypted bitmap of Tux is still recognizably Tux because pixel patterns survive.

questions.prompt: What is the SHA-256 of the empty string, in lowercase hex?
questions.explanation: The SHA-256 of an empty input is a fixed, well-known constant — useful as a sanity check for hash implementations.
